subject.title: Bug: 180s compaction timeout is a single wall clock over the whole chunk pipeline with no partial-progress reuse, so a legitimately-long compaction fails identically every turn

question: When a compaction timeout occurs after a valid partial or first-pass summary exists, should OpenClaw commit that safe result and continue, or require the full quality-guard pipeline to complete before changing session state?
rationale: The issue presents live evidence for both blocked sessions and a timeout reported after a context reduction; selecting the durable session-state contract is a maintainer product and correctness decision, not a mechanical retry change.

options.title: Commit the last safe summary
options.body: Persist a validated first-pass or completed-chunk result when later optional quality work exceeds the aggregate timeout, then report the degraded outcome accurately.

options.title: Require full quality completion
options.body: Keep the current all-or-nothing session update rule, but make timeout recovery and user guidance explicit while accepting that very long sessions may remain blocked.

recommendation.title: Commit the last safe summary
recommendation.body: Persist a validated first-pass or completed-chunk result when later optional quality work exceeds the aggregate timeout, then report the degraded outcome accurately.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked open repair proposal is the closest active implementation context, though repository-history ownership could not be verified in the unavailable shell.
